title: Treatment-resistant depression
bottleneck: Roughly a third of depressed patients do not respond to multiple antidepressant trials; existing drugs take weeks to work and target monoamines, a decades-old hypothesis, while the biology of resistance, spanning glutamate signaling, inflammation, and circuit dysfunction, is incompletely mapped.
why_it_blocks: Depression is the leading cause of disability worldwide; treatment resistance concentrates suicide risk and chronic suffering.
current_state: Ketamine, esketamine, and psychedelic-assisted therapies offer rapid relief for some resistant patients, but durability, access, and long-term safety questions remain. A reliably effective, durable treatment for resistant depression does not exist, and reviewers increasingly urge alternative modalities across neuropsychiatry. The rapid-acting treatments offer hope, but their effects often fade and long-term safety is unclear. Understanding the circuits and molecular drivers of resistance could finally move depression treatment beyond the monoamine era.
